title: reclaim's deletion-time re-proof only narrows the joining-child loss: a live child writing after the second comparison still loses its turn
mechanism_summary: `proveEntryStillGoes` and the following `unlink` are two operations, so a child that joined after enumeration and holds its own lease can write between them and have that write deleted with `reclaimed: 1, errors: []`; a live symlink replaced by a unique regular file is never re-proved at all.

finder_sections.text: 2. **P1 — deletion-time reproof only narrows the native joining-child loss.** [`proveEntryStillGoes` and its following `unlink`, `gc-cli.ts:1604–1622,1705–1719`](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/336f3360d6cf82450717b2c8b1417ed440e40f40/packages/coding-agent/src/cli/gc-cli.ts#L1604-L1622) are two operations. A real native child joins *after the parent enumerated the tree*, holds its own lease, and has its original bytes copied to the archive. At the **second** comparison of that child's own file I let it write `UNIQUE R13 NATIVE TURN` before comparison returns. [The exact-process witness](pinned/reclaim-join-r22.test.log) says `hit: true, checks: 2, reclaimed: 1, errors: [], restore: 0, recovered: false`; the only copy of that turn is gone. An earlier injection before the second proof now refuses part-way and keeps the turn ([control](pinned/controls-r15.test.log)); that is the measurable narrowing, not closure. A further [non-regular path witness](pinned/reclaim-link-r22.test.log) starts with an ordinary live symlink and changes it to a regular unique `UNIQUE TURN` immediately before `unlink`: the reproof function explicitly skips `!entry.compared`, and returns `reclaimed: 1, errors: []` with that file gone. The body admits the joined-child gap, but the changelog's unqualified "proves each entry once more through a descriptor" does not describe links/devices.

real_because.quote: **Reclaim cannot be fixed by re-proving.** A real child holding **its own lease** wrote `UNIQUE R13 NATIVE TURN` immediately after the second, deletion-time comparison; reclaim returned `reclaimed: 1, errors: []` and the restore came back without it. Replacing a live symlink with a unique regular file before its unlink lost that file the same way. There is always a gap between the proof and the `unlink`, so narrowing it is not a fix. **Reclaim must not delete what another live lease covers — report and skip.** A dead owner writes nothing late; a live one is not yours to reclaim.

mechanism: joining child|joins|native child|own lease|claimSession|another live lease

title: the artifact ownership scan follows a symlink to a FIFO and drains it, consuming a user's bytes during archive and even during a reclaim preview

It does not first require a regular file. The header reader opens with `"r"`, which blocks on a FIFO without a writer.' (line 20). The closest text about the artifact scan is the test-coverage note 'Missing FIFO and publication-read diagnostic coverage.' (line 124). The report never names `collectSessionFiles`, `leaseTranscripts` or `readArtifactSessionId`, and never states that input is consumed. Round 5 measured the same six static special-file cases on this head and got the same exits, so the defect was present at b084dd8d and both of this round's arms missed it (only the astra arm ran).

## R5-F1 — P2: Do not read special-file streams while checking artifact session ownership

**Locations:** `packages/coding-agent/src/cli/gc-cli.ts:2364-2371`, `2385-2388`, `2412-2424`. Reclaim's subsequent treatment of symlinks is at `1979-1997`.

`collectSessionFiles` scans with `onlyFiles: true, followSymlinks: true`. Bun includes a symlink whose target is a FIFO. `leaseTranscripts` then calls `readArtifactSessionId` on it. That helper starts with:

```ts
await Bun.file(file).slice(0, HEADER_SNIFF_BYTES).text()
```

There is no descriptor-based regular-file check. `O_NONBLOCK` alone is not enough: Bun can open the pipe nonblocking and then await input in `.text()`. The later `readSessionHeaderId` is not needed to trigger this defect.

real_because.quote: **`gc-cli.ts:2386`: the ownership scan does `Bun.file(file).slice(...).text()` without checking the opened object is a regular file, and Bun's glob includes symlinks to FIFOs.**

`browser-relay-tab-isolation.test.ts:110-116` and `browser-relay-detach.test.ts` launch Chromium themselves

claimed_by.text:
My first overlay commands had two harness errors: placing `--preload` before `test` selected the repository's broad package test script; after correcting the command order, a broad async loader returned undefined for unrelated modules.
